title: CORS, HTTPS, CSP and the OWASP Top 10 applied to APIs

videos.script: This is the last lesson, and it is about the edges of your API. {{edges}} Your API already checks who is asking and what they may do. But many of its users reach it through a browser. And a browser has rules of its own. {{browser}} You put a page on one address and the API on another. Then you watch the browser refuse to show the page what the API answered. {{refusal}} That refusal is the same-origin policy. CORS is how a server relaxes it, for the pages it trusts and no others. {{cors}} Then you encrypt the conversation. You make a certificate authority of your own, and watch curl refuse a server it cannot verify. {{https}} Last comes OWASP's list of the ten most common API mistakes. Each one has a defence, and almost every defence is a lesson of this course. The lesson ends with a checklist for the day your API goes live. {{owasp}}
